newsitem.title: USA: Farm Sec'y is Clinton speech "designated survivor".
newsitem.headline: Farm Sec'y is Clinton speech "designated survivor".

text.p: When the U.S. political elite assembles at the Capitol for President Bill Clinton's State of the Union address on Tuesday night, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman will be prepared to take over if disaster strikes.

Glickman, according to a White House official who did not wish to be identified, is designated survivor for the speech, taking his turn in a macabre rotation that ensures that someone in the national leadership will be left to carry on if all those at Clinton's speech are somehow wiped out.

The practice of designating one member of the president's Cabinet to stay away from an occasion of state as a national security precaution dates from the darkest days of the Cold War, when it was feared a gathering of the nation's leaders might present a tempting target for a surprise nuclear attack.
Decapitation, the doomsday term for eliminating a nation's leadership structure, remains a threat because of terrorism.

Glickman, 52, a nine-term veteran of Congress who has been in Clinton's Cabinet since 1994, is eighth in the line of succession for the presidency behind Vice President Al Gore, House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, Senate President pro tem Strom Thurmond and four more senior Cabinet members.
